subject: Insurance
title: Occupation Risk Classes
description: A micro-lesson that makes Occupation Risk Classes usable.

hook.text: Crab fishermen pay 5-10 times more for life insurance than office workers.

buildup.text: Insurers classify occupations by risk tier. Pilots, miners, and loggers sit at the top. Accountants sit near the bottom.

discovery.text: Some occupations are declined entirely. Active military in combat zones often can't buy standard policies at any price.

twist.text: Remote work lowered premiums for millions. A construction manager who moved to a desk job saw rates drop at renewal.

climax.text: Insurance prices what you do, not just who you are. Every career choice carries a mortality premium.

punchline.text: Office worker or crab fisherman? Your job title sets your rate.

quiz.question: Which occupation would have the highest life insurance premiums?
